story_of_day.headline: Revenge attacks spread from Narail as Dhaka blames India
story_of_day.story: After Awami League activists attacked a BNP procession in Narail and killed two BNP leaders, mobs torched dozens of homes and shops in Kalia, many belonging to Awami League members. Yunus's ancestral home in Chattogram was also set on fire. The prime minister says India is trying to destabilise Bangladesh, and a PM aide says Delhi is 'facilitating' an Awami League–Jamaat campaign against the BNP. India says it wants constructive ties and has stayed quiet on the politics.
story_of_day.so_what: The violence is feeding itself, and now it is also a fight with India. Hasina's planned return makes every new attack harder to calm.

last_time.text: Two BNP leaders had just been killed in Narail and 300 police were under investigation. The reprisals have now hit Kalia, and the blame has moved to India.

cards.headline: Iran says it shot down US drones over Hormuz as war talks stay stuck
cards.story: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say they downed US drones over the Strait, and Tehran repeated its conditions for reopening it. Washington answered with sanctions on four Iranians it calls 'oil trustees'. In Yemen the Saudi-led coalition hit Houthi sites in Hodeida, Sanaa, Saada and Taiz, and the Houthis threatened Saudi ports, airports and power stations. In Taiz, people have been cut off for weeks.
cards.so_what: No sign of a deal, and a second front is opening in the Red Sea. Oil is still falling only because Gulf barrels keep reaching Asia.

last_time.text: Iraq's militias and Hodeida were the new fronts. Now Iran is shooting at US drones and the Houthis are naming Saudi targets.

cards.money_angle: Brent closed at $89.95, up from $89.22. China's October crude imports from the Gulf rose 42% to a wartime high, which is why prices are soft.

cards.headline: Garment unrest in Ashulia: 80 factories shut and 96 arrested
cards.story: Wage protests turned violent in Savar-Ashulia and 80 factories closed. Police say 96 people were arrested, including five labour leaders, over arson and attacks on officers. Amnesty International says it is worried about the arrests of union leaders. A new wage scale is due from 1 December.
cards.so_what: Garments are the country's export engine. Arresting union leaders before the new scale starts risks more strikes just as political violence rises.

last_time.text: The new wage scale from 1 December was announced. Workers' anger has now spilled into the streets.

cards.headline: Xi calls the Australia–China relationship a 'turnaround'
cards.story: Xi Jinping praised a 'turnaround' in ties with Australia after talks with Anthony Albanese on the sidelines of APEC. Albanese is also set to meet Premier Li Qiang. In Washington, Trump touted his meetings with Xi and Putin, but NPR says he offered little in real results beyond a joint statement.
cards.so_what: Beijing is courting middle powers while the US-China deal stays thin. For Australia, warmer trade ties help, but they sit next to a US chip fight that is hardening.

last_time.text: California subpoenaed Nvidia and new US curbs froze chip shipments to Southeast Asia. Beijing is smiling at Canberra while that fight continues.

cards.headline: Zelensky calls Kyiv's Crimean Bridge strikes a 'fair response'
cards.story: Zelensky says Ukraine acted after 109 Russian aerial attacks on bridges inside Ukraine. He also called Putin a 'killer' after Trump described the Russian leader as a friend with a 'great relationship'. Poland says the Russian missiles that hit its territory were a deliberate provocation, but the bar for NATO's collective defence clause stays high.
cards.so_what: Kyiv is hitting back at infrastructure, and Trump's warmth towards Putin leaves Europe to carry the response.

last_time.text: Denmark expelled a Russian attache and Trump's energy truce collapsed. Now Kyiv is explaining its own strikes.

watch.title: Hasina's return and the 1 December wage scale
watch.text: Whether the Kalia reprisals calm or spread, and whether garment strikes restart when the new wage scale takes effect.

takes_review.text: I said not to pay up for a Hormuz risk premium. Brent is $89.95 against $89.22 when I wrote it, well below the $100 line that would prove me wrong. Too early to call, but so far it has held.
